sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'Held-durable claims skipped structurally' (2026-05-15/17, artifact) states the state filter preserves committed/abandoned/durable rows generally but does not claim all-durable retention-sweep exemption; design corpus=claim-lifetime.md Definition/Invariants explicitly scope the retention-sweep exemption to committed-durable only ('the retention sweep skips committed-durable rows'), silent on abandoned-durable; code=DeleteResolvedOlderThan (postgres/claim_handles.go:277-281) deletes WHERE state IN ('committed','abandoned') AND (state='abandoned' OR lifetime='subgraph'), so abandoned-durable rows ARE deleted; doc=orphan-reaper.md:26 said 'durable, never reaped' with no committed/abandoned split.
note: claim-lifetime.md (independent design-corpus artifact, second-tier precedence) already establishes the exemption is committed-durable-only; code corroborates. Rewrote the terminal-rows invariant bullet to state only committed-durable rows are exempt from the retention sweep.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 2 (re-keying: sync keys on gRPC connection state, async keys on last_progress_at/dispatched_at vs per-row deadlines; re-assignment is the normal pending-queue claim path) and Required behaviors 'Quiet-period / runtime deadlines' (2026-06-16 055468fc + 2026-06-21 21306ffe, transcript, user: 'the new mechanism is quiet-period'); doc=orphan-reaper.md:11 said the reaper 'hard-deletes stale rows from the node-run ledger'; code=ReleaseClaim (queue.go:367) does UPDATE ... state='stale', not a delete, invoked by SweepExecutorDeadlines and runReapOrphanFrameDispatches; only claim-handle DeleteIfExpired hard-deletes.
note: Dossier's transcript-tier re-keying description is a release-for-reassignment model, not a delete, matching code. Rewrote 'What it is' to distinguish release (node-run, frame-dispatch) from hard-delete (claim-handle).

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 5 ('Sweeps keep split-by-purpose naming ... deliberately no unified single orphan reaper and no umbrella SweepOrphans') and Intentional absences ('A single unified orphan reaper: ... unification is documentation-level only', 2026-05-04 artifact; 'An umbrella SweepOrphans function: split-by-purpose naming is the convention', 2026-05-12 nomenclature-resolution, artifact) and Required behaviors naming SweepExecutorDeadlines and SweepOrphanedBlobs explicitly (transcript/artifact); code=scheduler.go tick() wires SweepExecutorDeadlines, SweepOrphanedClaimHandles, runReapOrphanFrameDispatches; no sweep named stale-recovery or ready exists; doc=orphan-reaper.md:11 enumerated 'stale-recovery, orphaned-node-run, ready, and orphaned-claim-handle sweeps'.
note: Dossier corroborated across transcript and artifact tiers that sweeps are split-by-purpose and never unified; combined with code, two of the four named family members are invented. Rewrote 'What it is' to describe the family by mechanism (node-run dispatch sweep, in-frame dispatch sweep, claim-handle sweep) without inventing names.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 6 ('The reaper's claim-handle candidate predicate is state=active AND expires_at < now()') and Intentional absences ('The claim-handle expires_at TTL math survives under the liveness vocabulary (liveness-extend, LivenessInterval, tickLiveness)', 2026-06-16/17 transcript) and Required behaviors 'Quiet-period / runtime deadlines' describing the distinct node-run mechanism (2026-06-16/21, transcript); code=ListExpired (claim_handles.go:399) cuts on expires_at set to Now+5*livenessInterval (~25s liveness lease, runner_acquire_claims.go:72), distinct from decideExecutorDeadlineRelease's absolute-runtime/quiet-period cutoff (conductor.go); doc=orphan-reaper.md:11/24 described the claim-handle cutoff as 'the per-dispatch absolute-deadline'.
note: Dossier corroborates two independent cutoff mechanisms (liveness-lease expiry for claim-handle vs quiet-period/absolute-runtime deadline for dispatches); doc conflated them into one description. Rewrote the cutoff prose in 'What it is' and the matching invariant bullet to state both mechanisms distinctly.

sources: dossier=same as row 486 (Net position bullet 6, Intentional absences liveness-lease note, Required behaviors quiet-period bullet); code=ListExpired cuts on expires_at (liveness lease) vs decideExecutorDeadlineRelease (conductor.go:87-113) cutting on effective_max_runtime_seconds/effective_max_quiet_period_seconds; doc=orphan-reaper.md:24 closing clause 'Claim-handle and node-run sweeps share the same cutoff' directly contradicted the preceding sentence in the same bullet.

Fixed in the same edit as row 486 (rewrote the whole cutoff invariant bullet to state the two mechanisms are distinct).

sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'Every reap path is claimant-guarded (invariant 4): no path removes a holder's row without holder verification' (general, applies to any reap path including frame-scoped ones) and 'Race-honest testing ... orphan-reaper vs in-flight-terminal overlap among the four defended seams' (2026-06-11, artifact) implying multiple reap seams beyond the two named in the doc; code=runReapOrphanFrameDispatches (engine.go:189) releases orphaned in-frame dispatches via the same ReleaseClaim path as the node-run sweep; frame.md's own Boundaries claims only frame-timeout warning emission and the ended_at stamp, not orphan-dispatch reaping, leaving that reap path unclaimed by either doc; doc=orphan-reaper.md adjacency list (l.19) omitted `frame` and 'What it is' omitted the in-frame release mechanism entirely.
note: Narrower than the original finding: frame.md already owns ended_at stamping and the advisory stuck-frame warning, so those should NOT be pulled into orphan-reaper.md (would duplicate ownership across two design docs). The genuine gap is that the in-frame orphan-dispatch release path is a reap path (per dossier's invariant-4 framing) with no owning mention in either doc. Added `frame` to the adjacency list and named the in-frame dispatch sweep alongside the node-run sweep in 'What it is', without claiming ended_at/stuck-frame-warning ownership. If frame.md's own adjacency list should reciprocally cite orphan-reaper, that edit is out of scope here (frame.md may not be touched by this task) and is flagged for a human follow-up.
